rationale: Several details of 17:1-5 have counterparts in Exodus 24:15-18: a time notice of six days, a mountain, a cloud, and a voice from the cloud. Matthew 17:1 opens "After six days"; Exodus 24:16 reads, "For six days the cloud covered it, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud" (BSB). A case-insensitive script finds "after six days" in this app's BSB only at Matthew 17:1 and Mark 9:2. In Greek, Matthew's meth' hēmeras hex shares the noun and the number with the Septuagint's hex hēmeras (Swete's text on Bible Hub), and both passages speak out of the cloud (ek tēs nephelēs at 17:5; ek mesou tēs nephelēs at Exodus 24:16). Matthew gives no formula and does not name Sinai, so the type is at most allusion. The label is plausible, not strong, because named readers make the link and named readers doubt it. The Catholic NABRE notes say the mountain is "possibly recalling the revelation to Moses on Mount Sinai," citing Exodus 24:12-18. Andrei Orlov reports Davies and Allison listing seven parallels, among them that "the event takes place 'after six days' (Exod 24.16; Mark 9.2)," and Craig Evans: "the chronological notation 'after six days' recalls Exod 24:16." Orlov also reports other explanations of the six days from Adela Yarbro Collins's survey (Wellhausen's resurrection reading, a Sabbath reading, and Foster McCurley's view that the phrase is a Semitic idiom), and he points to John McGuckin for criticism of the Sinai reading of the six days. These scholars are read here only through Orlov's chapter in Revelation and Leadership in the Kingdom of God (Gorgias Press, 2020). The commentaries on 17:1 collected on Bible Hub count the six days from Peter's confession and reconcile them with Luke's "About eight days" (Luke 9:28, BSB); none of them argues the Exodus 24 link, and Barnes on 17:5 cites Exodus 24:15-17 only as one example of the cloud as divine presence. The shining face and Exodus 34:29-35 are discussed in the lesson and not authored as a separate row.
